name: Returned address stored in a 32-bit slot
required_postconditions: the address the host returns round-trips through 32-bit storage

failure_sink.description: the case reports `lost`: mmap returned a valid, writable mapping whose address does not fit a 32-bit slot, so the program's stored pointer refers to unrelated memory

extraction_limitations: Single-claim contract written to pair with a ground-truth case. It asserts exactly one thing so that a whole-contract verdict can be compared against a single observation without ambiguity.
x_groundtruth: RS-VM-0013, and the seventh MVP demonstration: valid host operation rejected by caller assumption. mmap(NULL) always succeeds and always returns a valid mapping - the host does nothing wrong. The 32-bit pointer_storage_width is the program's, and on every 64-bit host the returned address is above 2^32, so a 32-bit slot cannot hold it. The real shape is LuaJIT without GC64 (RSC-0018) and MAP_32BIT-style assumptions (RSC-0020). Distinct from every other case here, which needs the host to refuse or relocate; this one needs the host to succeed.
